detail.title: Architectural Distinctions in Preference Formation
detail.summary: Long-term preference formation in autonomous agents is not solely a function of internal state adaptation but is constrained by hierarchical autonomy (global vs. local), explicit ethics-based auditing frameworks, and physical control constraints that dictate resilience. These structural layers separate transient behavioral responses from persistent decision-making preferences.
detail.reason: Incorporating findings on governance (EBA) and control constraints (CAV controllability) to refine the distinction between transient behavior and preference formation.
